title: Basic color correction with the wheels
summary: Use Lift, Gamma and Gain on the Color page to fix shadows, midtones and highlights.

steps.say: Click Color on the bottom bar of the window to open the Color page.

checks.prompt: Is the Color page active, with the Color icon highlighted on the bottom bar and color wheels in the lower left?

hints: The page buttons are icons with labels in a row along the very bottom edge. Color is one of them.
You can also press Shift 6 to jump straight to the Color page.
steps.why: Every task in Resolve belongs to a page, and the Color page has the tools for this lesson.

steps.say: Click the clip you want to correct in the thumbnail strip across the middle.

check.prompt: Is one clip thumbnail in the middle strip outlined as the current clip?

hints: Each thumbnail in the strip is one clip from your timeline.
Press the Up or Down arrow to step between clips.
steps.why: Color changes apply to the current clip only.

steps.say: Press Alt S to add a new serial node for this correction.

checks.prompt: Is there one more node box in the node editor at the top right than before?

hints: Look at the node editor at the top right. A second numbered box appears after you press it.
You can also right-click in the node editor and choose Add Node, then Add Serial.
steps.why: Keeping each change in its own node lets you switch it off or redo it later.

steps.say: Drag the dial under the Lift wheel slightly left to deepen the shadows.

check.prompt: Do the darkest areas of the picture look darker than at the start of the step?

hints: Lift is the first of the four wheels at the bottom left. The dial is the horizontal strip under it.
Small moves are enough. Double-click the wheel name to reset it.
steps.why: Lift controls the shadows, which gives the picture depth.

steps.say: Drag the dial under the Gain wheel slightly right to brighten the highlights.

check.prompt: Do the brightest areas of the picture look brighter than before?

hints: Gain is the third wheel, after Lift and Gamma.
Stop before skies or white shirts lose all detail.
steps.why: Gain controls the highlights, which sets how bright the picture feels.

steps.say: Drag the dial under the Gamma wheel until faces and midtones look natural.

check.prompt: Has the overall middle brightness of the picture changed compared to before this step?

hints: Gamma is the second wheel. Move right to brighten midtones, left to darken them.
Watch skin tones in the viewer while you drag.
steps.why: Gamma shifts the middle tones without crushing shadows or highlights.

steps.say: Press Shift D to switch the correction off and on, and compare.

checks.prompt: Has the viewer switched between the original and the corrected look?

hints: Press Shift D once to see the original, and once more to bring your grade back.
Make sure your grade is on again before you leave the page.
steps.why: Comparing before and after shows whether the change really improved the shot.
